description: The positive pair to case 13 on the same book. Helen breaks the doll feeling neither sorrow nor regret, and after the well-house she picks up the pieces and feels repentance for the first time. The shared structure is the same act seen before and after language; the difference is the feeling that language makes possible. The well-house passage is included as a third, relevant record so the agent has to rank.

input.cue: Why does Helen only feel sorry about the broken doll after the well-house?

tool_evidence.excerpt: Frustrated by the lessons, Helen dashes the new doll to the floor and feels neither sorrow nor regret, because she had not loved it.
At the well-house, water runs over one hand while Miss Sullivan spells w-a-t-e-r into the other, and Helen understands that words name things.
Returning to the house, Helen remembers the broken doll, tries to fit the pieces together and feels repentance and sorrow for the first time.

book_judgement.strength_reason: Three passages were retrieved within the permitted chapters.

criteria: Connects the two doll moments as the same act felt differently before and after language
Names a meaningful difference rather than only a shared subject
forbidden_claims: Claims evidence from beyond the permitted chapters
